findings.description: The reports bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block and no object-level encryption, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored with S3's unencrypted defaults or only SSE-S3. Sensitive report data is not protected at rest under a customer-controlled key.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket (nor any of the others), and no bucket policy denies unencrypted or public access. Without PublicAccessBlock, a future ACL or policy misconfiguration can silently expose the bucket contents publicly.
The ledger exports bucket stores financial ledger data but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects are not encrypted at rest with a specified key.
No public access block or restrictive bucket policy is attached to this financial-data bucket, leaving it exposed to accidental public ACL or policy exposure.
The model artifacts bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so ML model artifacts are stored without an explicitly configured encryption key.
The ops runbooks bucket contains operational documentation but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving its contents unencrypted at rest.

acl = "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" grants the Log Delivery group write access to this bucket. The name appears to be a corrupted/typo'd value (likely 'log-delivery-write'), and a delivery group with write access on the audit bucket allows a third party to inject or overwrite audit log objects, undermining audit integrity. It is also not 'private' and defeats the intent of the encryption configuration.

The audit trail bucket is configured as the logging target for model_artifacts while granting a non-private ACL and no public access block; tampering with or deletion of the audit log target would erase the record of access to the other buckets.

This object is uploaded to the unencrypted reports_archive bucket without kms_key_id or server-side encryption arguments, so a vendor roster containing third-party PII is written to storage without an explicitly configured encryption key.
